mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such Fed rate spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is expected to boost investor confidence, driving a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening below structural unemployment rate
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant deviation from the prior 30-day average during such labor market events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A month-on-month increase in the HOUST index (retail sales) of at least 3% is a leading indicator of consumer demand recovery, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Rebound in consumer demand after contraction
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after such an HOUST surge (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) of 2% or more suggests supply-side resilience, which should correlate with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 30-day baseline during such INDPRO expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% indicate disinflation, which should produce a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return if the trend persists.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for two consecutive months and remains below 2.0%
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain flat or negative despite sustained CPIAUCSL declines (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) by over 10,000 in a month signals labor market expansion, which should drive a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return when coupled with rising UNRATE.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in a single month and UNRATE < 7.0%
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically positive during such combined labor indicators (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RSAFS (retail sales of big box stores) by 5% or more in two consecutive months indicates weakening demand, predicting a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Persistent weakness in large retail demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows by at least 3% in the quarter ending the month before prediction, it reflects robust economic activity and should be associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return in expanding regimes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns underperform a 10-day baseline during such GDP growth (p > 0.05).
